name: Medial Plantar Nerve Entrapment / Jogger's Foot
tags: medial plantar nerve entrapment / jogger's foot
definition: Compression of the medial plantar nerve causing burning pain or numbness in the medial arch and plantar forefoot, often in runners.

investigations.principle: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; electrodiagnostics or ultrasound are selective.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, tendon, cartilage, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Persistent focal entrapment may require specialist decompression.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Pada Vata-neuralgic phenotype may be documented.

patientEducation.summary: Compression of the medial plantar nerve causing burning pain or numbness in the medial arch and plantar forefoot, often in runners.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, major trauma, severe deformity, progressive weakness, tendon rupture, infection or other listed red flags.
